title: Campaign
description: A named study: the set of artifacts that together answer one question. Tools produce artifacts and provenance chains explain each one, but the STUDY -- these datasets, these calibrations, these competing fits, this designed next experiment, as one unit with a goal -- was previously nobody's record; it existed only as whatever a pipeline script happened to do. A campaign record makes the composition itself registrable, checkable, and diagrammable. DRAFT (2026-08): added on the real-data-revision branch for the September meeting to accept or overrule, alongside the other changes the real data forced.

schema_version.description: The schema version this document was written against.

campaign_id.description: Stable, human-chosen identifier, e.g. 'coox-b29-prbs'. Not content-addressed: a campaign accretes members over its life, and its identity is the QUESTION, not the bytes.

description.description: What question this campaign exists to answer, in a sentence or two.

status.description: abandoned is a legal, honest state; deleting the record of a study that fizzled is how the same dead end gets explored twice.

artifacts.description: The campaign's members, each with the role it plays. Same shape as publication.artifacts, deliberately: one referencing convention means one implementation of reference-checking (tcat-index's referenced_ids) covers both. List the ROOTS -- fits, designs, reports; their full lineage is reachable through provenance and does not need re-listing.

ref.description: An artifact id, an art:// reference, a dataset_id, or a model_id.

kind.description: Which registry to resolve `ref` against. 'external' names something outside this project, which must still be named rather than implied.

role.description: What this member IS to the campaign: 'baseline fit', 'topology control', 'designed next experiment'. Free text; the roles are the campaign's own vocabulary.

milestone.description: The project milestone this campaign serves, when there is one. Free text: a milestone identifier means whatever the project that set it says it means, and this standard does not define any.

spokes.description: The repositories whose data and tools this campaign runs on. Since 0.3.0 an entry may be the PINNED identity a tool spoke ran at -- name, contract version and source digest -- which makes the campaign record a lockfile: 'which code produced this study' is answerable from the record without walking every artifact, and installing what it names reproduces it. A bare string is still accepted (a data spoke has no version to pin, and older records name spokes by name only).

name.description: The spoke or tool repository, e.g. 'tcat-fit'.

version.description: Contract version the campaign ran with.

digest.description: Normalised source digest the campaign ran with; matches provenance tool.source_digest on its artifacts.

notes.description: Anything a future reader needs that no structured field carries.

maturity.description: How much weight someone else may put on this record. Absent means `sandbox`, which is true of everything written before the field existed.

freeze.description: PRESENT means the campaign is FROZEN: it is checked against its own pins, never against the toolchain's main, so tools may move without making it stale. Its absence means the campaign tracks main as before. Freezing is a recorded decision, and so is unfreezing (`tcat-campaign unfreeze` removes this block and notes why). A frozen campaign must be complete or abandoned: a study still being developed has no single toolchain to be frozen at.

reason.description: Why: published, dormant, too expensive to keep re-running. Read by whoever wants to unfreeze it.

environment.description: Repository-relative path of the environment lock written at freeze time: the exact commits of every TransientCatalysis package and the exact versions of every third-party dependency the pins resolve to. The pins say WHICH code produced the study; the lock is how that code is installed again after its main has moved on.

held.description: Notebooks HELD at the toolchain they last ran on, inside a campaign that otherwise tracks main: expensive exhibits that are not re-executed every time a pinned tool moves. A held notebook is checked against its own `tools`, not the campaign pins, and must still have run on exactly those; the check reports it as held rather than passing it silently. Release a hold to bring the notebook back under the pins (which then usually means re-executing it).

notebook.description: Repository-relative path of the committed notebook.

reason.description: Why it is held, e.g. 'about 6 h on 32 cores; re-run when the axial solver settles'.

name.description: The tool or library repository, as in a `spokes` pin.

version.description: Contract version the notebook ran with.

digest.description: Source digest the notebook ran with; matches provenance tool.source_digest.

tools.description: The identities the notebook ran on when it was held, one per pinned tool or library it records.
